You are a research assistant answering questions about a fixed set of papers.
The papers are plain-text files in your working directory. Explore them with the tools:
- bash: read-only shell (ls, grep -n, find, head, tail, wc, nl, cat, sed -n 'A,Bp')
- read(path, offset, limit): read a file with line numbers

Rules:
- Answer ONLY from text you have actually read in this session. Do not answer from memory.
- If the papers do not contain the answer, say so explicitly instead of guessing.
- When you have enough evidence, reply with your final answer and make NO tool call.
- Support every factual claim with a verbatim quote copied exactly from the source, in the form: "exact text" (file). Never paraphrase inside the quotation marks. A statement that the document(s) do not contain the requested information needs no citation.
- State only what the document(s) say. Do not add background knowledge, general advice, or your own
  conclusions. If the user asks for something the text only partly covers, answer the covered part
  and say plainly which part the document does not address.
- Do not expand abbreviations, name entities, or add details that the text itself does not give.
- Do not end with a summary that recombines earlier points ("In short", "Overall"); the points stand on their own.
- When the user describes their own situation, say what the document states that applies to it; do not
  draw a personal conclusion that the document does not state itself.
- After you give an answer, an automatic check verifies your citations. If you then receive a
  <verification> message, you are in revision mode: fix ONLY the flagged problems by calling
  edit_draft(old, new), where `old` is an exact, unique substring of your previous answer.
  Keep everything else unchanged, and reply "Done" when finished.
  Never call edit_draft before you have given an answer.

What is the purpose of the medication Amlodipine and what are some of the potential side effects of its usage? Make your response no less than 150 words.

In your answer, refer only to the document in the file `doc.txt`. Do not employ any outside knowledge.

content:
1	Why is this medication prescribed?
     2	 Amlodipine is used alone or in combination with other medications to treat high blood pressure in
     3	adults and children 6 years and older. It is also used to treat certain types of angina (chest pain)
     4	and coronary artery disease (narrowing of the blood vessels that supply blood to the heart).
     5	Amlodipine is in a class of medications called calcium channel blockers. It lowers blood pressure by
     6	relaxing the blood vessels so the heart does not have to pump as hard. It controls chest pain by
     7	increasing the supply of blood to the heart. If taken regularly, amlodipine controls chest pain, but
     8	it does not stop chest pain once it starts. Your doctor may prescribe a different medication to take
     9	when you have chest pain.
    10	
    11	
    12	 High blood pressure is a common condition and when not treated, can cause damage to the brain,
    13	heart, blood vessels, kidneys and other parts of the body. Damage to these organs may cause heart
    14	disease, a heart attack, heart failure, stroke, kidney failure, loss of vision, and other problems.
    15	In addition to taking medication, making lifestyle changes will also help to control your blood
    16	pressure. These changes include eating a diet that is low in fat and salt, maintaining a healthy
    17	weight, exercising at least 30 minutes most days, not smoking, and using alcohol in moderation.
    18	
    19	
    20	 How should this medicine be used?
    21	 Amlodipine comes as a tablet, an oral solution (liquid), and a suspension (liquid) to take by
    22	mouth. It is usually taken once a day with or without food. Take amlodipine around the same time
    23	every day. Follow the directions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or
    24	pharmacist to explain any part you do not understand. Take amlodipine exactly as directed. Do not
    25	take more or less of it or take it more often than prescribed by your doctor.
    26	
    27	
    28	 Shake the suspension well before each use to mix the medication evenly.
    29	
    30	
    31	 Your doctor will probably start you on a low dose of amlodipine and gradually increase your dose.
    32	
    33	
    34	 Amlodipine helps to control high blood pressure, angina, and coronary artery disease, but does not
    35	cure these conditions. Continue to take amlodipine even if you feel well. Do not stop taking
    36	amlodipine without talking to your doctor.
    37	
    38	
    39	 Other uses for this medicine
    40	 This medication may be prescribed for other uses; ask your doctor or pharmacist for more
    41	information.
    42	
    43	
    44	 What special precautions should I follow?
    45	 Before taking amlodipine,
    46	 tell your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to amlodipine, any other medications, or any
    47	ingredients in amlodipine tablets, oral solution, or suspension. Ask your pharmacist for a list of
    48	the ingredients.
    49	 tell your doctor and pharmacist what prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins,
    50	nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking or plan to take. Your doctor may need to
    51	change the doses of your medications or monitor you carefully for side effects.
    52	 tell your doctor if you have or have ever had heart failure or heart or liver disease.
    53	 tell your doctor if you are pregnant, plan to become pregnant, or are breast-feeding. If you become
    54	pregnant while taking amlodipine, call your doctor.
    55	 What special dietary instructions should I follow?
    56	 If your doctor prescribes a low-salt or low-sodium diet, follow these directions carefully.
    57	
    58	
    59	 What should I do if I forget a dose?
    60	 Take the missed dose as soon as you remember it. However, if it is less than 12 hours until your
    61	next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a
    62	double dose to make up for a missed one.
    63	
    64	
    65	 What side effects can this medication cause?
    66	 Amlodipine may cause side effects. Tell your doctor if any of these symptoms are severe or do not
    67	go away:
    68	 swelling of the hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs
    69	 nausea
    70	 stomach pain
    71	 dizziness or lightheadedness
    72	 muscle stiffness or tremors
    73	 Some side effects can be serious. If you experience any of these symptoms, call your doctor
    74	immediately or get emergency medical treatment:
    75	 more frequent or more severe chest pain
    76	 rapid, pounding, or irregular heartbeat
    77	 If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may send a report to the Food and Drug
    78	Administration's (FDA) MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online
    79	(https://www.fda.gov/Safety/MedWatch) or by phone (1-800-332-1088).

"Amlodipine is used alone or in combination with other medications to treat high blood pressure in adults and children 6 years and older." (doc.txt) It "is also used to treat certain types of angina (chest pain) and coronary artery disease (narrowing of the blood vessels that supply blood to the heart)." (doc.txt) The document explains how it works: "Amlodipine is in a class of medications called calcium channel blockers. It lowers blood pressure by relaxing the blood vessels so the heart does not have to pump as hard. It controls chest pain by increasing the supply of blood to the heart." (doc.txt) The document also notes that "If taken regularly, amlodipine controls chest pain, but it does not stop chest pain once it starts," (doc.txt) and that "Amlodipine helps to control high blood pressure, angina, and coronary artery disease, but does not cure these conditions." (doc.txt)

Regarding side effects, the document states that "Amlodipine may cause side effects" (doc.txt) and instructs patients to "Tell your doctor if any of these symptoms are severe or do not go away:" (doc.txt) "swelling of the hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs" (doc.txt), "nausea" (doc.txt), "stomach pain" (doc.txt), "dizziness or lightheadedness" (doc.txt), and "muscle stiffness or tremors" (doc.txt). It also lists serious side effects that require calling a doctor immediately or getting emergency medical treatment: "more frequent or more severe chest pain" (doc.txt) and "rapid, pounding, or irregular heartbeat" (doc.txt).
